sentences.text: The daily planning cycle begins with a pre-tactical baseline prepared each morning before the main bank structure is locked for operational use.
The Regional Flow Manager owns the baseline process and confirms that the planning horizon, cutover time, and review checkpoints are understood by the participating operational roles.
The Regional Flow Platform creates the initial demand picture from published schedules, approved seasonal allocations, overnight schedule changes, and received Flight Intent Message data.
The Flight Data Exchange normalizes flight identifiers, aircraft types, routing fields, and planned operating times so that later comparisons use a single reference record.
The Demand Prediction Service converts the normalized schedule into expected arrival and departure demand by time band, runway direction, terminal area, and major traffic flow.
The Airline Operations Coordinator reviews material deviations from filed intent, including aircraft swaps, early cancellations, recovery flights, and known connection protection actions.
The Aircraft Operator Representative validates that operator priorities are visible where they are allowed by the Business Rules Registry and local coordination agreements.
The Meteorology Briefing Officer provides the morning weather outlook with emphasis on wind trend, ceiling, visibility, convective risk, temperature limits, and confidence over the planning horizon.
The Weather Ingest Gateway makes the outlook available to the Capacity Assessment Module and preserves the forecast issue time for audit and later performance review.
The Airspace Sector Planner declares expected sector constraints, route availability assumptions, and any planned staffing limitations that could influence arrival or departure metering.
The Military Airspace Liaison confirms whether shared airspace assumptions remain valid for the morning and identifies any conditional availability that must be treated as uncertain.
The Tower Supervisor sends the Runway Inspection Note before the first planning consolidation window.

The Tower Supervisor also declares anticipated runway configuration, usable operating length assumptions, and any local sequencing constraints that affect the North Runway Meter and South Runway Meter.
The Airport Duty Manager confirms terminal opening status, essential facility readiness, and airport service constraints that may affect the first operational waves.
The Ramp Control Lead reviews early stand readiness using information from the Ramp Movement Board, East Apron Sensor, West Apron Sensor, and handling coordination calls.
The Ground Handling Dispatcher confirms whether planned handling teams and equipment coverage are sufficient for the expected concentration of turns in each apron area.
The Handling Resource Planner compares the demand curve with available ground resources and flags time bands where aircraft turn performance is likely to reduce stand availability.

The Capacity Assessment Module combines the runway declaration, weather outlook, airspace constraints, stand readiness, and ground resource assumptions into a proposed Airport Acceptance Rate by period.
The proposed Airport Acceptance Rate is tested against the demand profile to identify overloads, underused capacity, and points where a Ground Delay Program may become necessary.
The Slot Coordinator uses the Slot Allocation Engine to prepare an initial slot feasibility view but does not publish binding Calculated Takeoff Time values during baseline construction.
The Departure Metering Service estimates provisional Target Off Block Time sensitivity so planners can see how small changes in capacity would affect stand occupancy and departure queues.
The Arrival Regulation Console highlights inbound demand periods where holding, speed control, or upstream sequencing may be needed if the forecast capacity materializes.
The Digital Briefing Room displays the emerging Airport Capacity Plan and records unresolved assumptions in the Collaborative Decision Log for confirmation during the morning coordination briefing.

The Common Situation Display presents the approved pre-tactical baseline as the shared reference for Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, and early Recovery Phase decisions.

When the baseline is approved, the Alert Distribution Hub notifies participating roles that the morning plan is available and that changes must be entered through controlled Regional Flow Platform functions.
The Performance Analytics Warehouse retains the baseline inputs, capacity declarations, and approval timestamps so the Post Operations Report can compare planned performance with actual outcomes.
